analyses.content: 录音提到盐在人类健康中扮演着不可或缺的角色，原文的“indispensable role”直接对应题目中的“essential”，因此填health。
你可能会听到前一句的“basic human tastes”想要填tastes，但这里题目问的是盐对什么来说是“essential（必不可少的）”，对应的是“indispensable role”，所以重点信息是health。
The taste of salt is one of the basic human tastes. More importantly, salt plays an indispensable role in the health of human beings.
录音明确说到拉丁语“salarium argentum”演变成了英语单词“salary”，完美对应题干表述的来源关系。
你可能听到前面的“soldier's pay”想要填pay，但题目问的是哪个词是从拉丁语演变来的，你需要向后听找到明确表示派生关系的“derived the English word salary”。
A soldier's pay, which partly consisted of salt, was known as salarium argentum in Latin, from which we derived the English word salary.
录音说到瑞典家庭夏天会在周围的森林（surrounding forests）里养动物，原文的“surrounding”对应题目中的“local”，因此填forests。
你可能听到summer或weather想要填进去，但题目问的是把动物养在“哪里（in the local...）”，你需要抓取表示地点的名词forests。
In order to ensure the supply of meat, many families in Sweden began to raise animals in the surrounding forests during the summer when the weather was suitable for animals to survive.
录音直接提到十月（October）是古代瑞典人桌上有新鲜肉的唯一月份，完美对应题目的“only available in”。
录音前文提到了“three to four months”，你可能想直接把数字当答案填，但这是指喂养的时间长度，你需要往后听，找到具体指出哪个月份才有鲜肉的October。

These animals were fed every day until about three to four months later. That's in October, they were ready to be butchered for meat, and that was the only month when ancient Swedish people had fresh meat on their table.
录音提到历史文献记录了瑞典国王（king）的日常饮食（everyday meals），“everyday meals”对应题目中的“diet”，所以填king。
录音里紧接着出现了很多干扰数字（175、150）和meat等信息，但题目问的是“谁（the...）”的饮食，你在听到表示所属关系的“Swedish king's”时就要快速抓取核心名词king。

There was evidence that salt was widely used to preserve meat. Historical documents in fifteen seventy-three recorded the Swedish king's everyday meals, mentioning that one hundred and seventy-five pounds of meat was consumed each year, but over one hundred and fifty pounds was salty. From this, we can clearly see the importance of salt in Sweden at that time.
录音提到啤酒（beer）的年销量飙升，并且这和食物里盐分过高有关，原文的“soared”对应题目的“increased rapidly”，因此填beer。
你可能会一直沉浸在上一句关于meat的话题中，但录音用“In addition（此外）”引出了新的并列信息，此时你的注意力必须跟着转移，去听是什么东西销量上涨了（beer）。
In addition, the documents also noted the annual sales of beer in Sweden soared during that period, and this must be related to high levels of salt in their food.
录音先提到两个最重要的盐来源是oceans和basins，接着补充说明后者（即basins）的底部通常是沙漠（deserts），在那里可以找到盐，因此填deserts。
录音前面像报菜名一样说了好几种来源（seawater, mineral deposits等），你容易在这里迷失，你必须耐心等到对应题干信息的oceans和basins出现后，再去抓取具体描述basins内部地形的名词deserts。

It has long been found that salt can be extracted from seawater, mineral deposits, saline lakes, brine, spring, etc., among which the two most important ones are oceans and basins. On the floor of the latter often lie deserts where traces of salt can be found, such as the Sahara.
录音在说明了海水盐含有杂质之后，对比指出泉水盐（spring water）几乎没有杂质，且含盐量更加浓缩（more concentrated），对应题目要求。
你可能会听到前面的purified或者impurities就急着填，但这是在形容海水的特点或处理方式，而题干问的是泉水盐比海水盐更“怎么样”，你需要紧抓“more”后面的形容词concentrated。

For example, salt from seawater is always mixed with impurities, so after the salt is dried, the sediments and other chemicals need to be purified before eating. However, this is not the case with salt from spring water. We can hardly find any impurities, and the salt level is much more concentrated.
录音指出瑞典人为了保证进口盐的供应，必须非常重视航运（shipping）并保护其完好无损，原文的“keep it undamaged”对应题目中的“protect”，因此填shipping。
你可能会听到前面的countries或者abroad想要填进去，但题干问的是要保护“什么途径或方式（By which...）”，你要定位到能够被“undamaged（无损）”修饰的词汇shipping。

Because of the heavy use of salt in the diet, Sweden could not feed itself and had to import large amounts of salt from other countries. In order to make sure they could buy enough salt from abroad, the Swedish had to attach great importance to shipping and keep it undamaged, as it was the most crucial way at that time.
录音提到那些背着盐走的人逐渐被认为是早期的一种交通运输方式（a mode of transport），原文的“a mode of”直接对应题目中的“a natural means of”，因此填transport。
录音里大篇幅描述了人们背着盐走（shoulders or backs），你可能想填一个具体的身体部位或动作，但题目宏观地问这是“一种……的方式（a means of）”，你需要向后听总结句里的“a mode of transport”。

While in other ancient countries, in order to distribute salt to other places, groups of men were employed. They put bags of salt on their shoulders or backs and moved them to the surrounding regions. And gradually, these people were considered as a mode of transport in early times.
